title: Nachos Supreme
subtitle: Tortilla chips loaded with beef, beans, cheese, and all the toppings
excerpt: Tortilla chips layered with spiced beef, black beans, and cheese, baked until the cheese melts, then loaded with guacamole, soured cream, jalapeños, and salsa. Serves a crowd as a starter or informal sharing plate.
sourceNotes: Loaded nachos (nachos supreme): an American Tex-Mex stadium food and restaurant dish, developed from the original nachos created by Ignacio 'Nacho' Anaya in Piedras Negras, Mexico in 1943. The fully loaded version with beef, beans, guacamole, and soured cream became a US restaurant staple from the 1970s.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The beef filling can be made a day ahead. Assemble and bake just before serving; nachos go soggy if left.

content.text: Nachos supreme are a baking tray of tortilla chips covered in spiced beef, black beans, and cheese, baked until the cheese melts and bubbles, then finished with cold toppings at the table. The key is layering: chips, then beef and beans, then cheese, so the cheese covers the filling and the chips underneath stay crisp as long as possible. Add the cold toppings after baking, not before.

items.prepNote: bought tortilla chips, or corn tortillas cut into triangles and baked at 180°C for 10-12 minutes until crisp
mashed with lime juice and salt

content.text: A large baking tray gives the chips enough room to stay in a single layer. Crowded chips steam each other and go soft.

Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil in a frying pan. Cook {{onion}} finely chopped onion for 5 minutes. Add {{garlic}} of crushed garlic for 1 minute. Add {{beef-mince}} of beef mince; cook 5-6 minutes until browned. Stir in the chilli powder and cumin, season with salt, and cook 2 minutes. Stir in the drained black beans. Keep the filling fairly dry; drain any excess liquid.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Spread the tortilla chips in a single layer across a large baking tray.
Spoon the beef and bean mixture evenly over the chips. Scatter the grated cheddar generously over the top. Bake for 8-10 minutes until the cheese has melted and is beginning to bubble.
Remove from the oven. Add the cold toppings straight away: spoonfuls of mashed avocado and soured cream, diced tomato, sliced jalapeño, and coriander. Serve immediately with lime wedges.

items.cause: Too much moisture in the filling, or cold toppings added before baking
items.fix: Keep the beef filling dry; drain excess fat and liquid before spreading on the chips. Add all cold toppings after the oven, not before.

items.symptom: Bottom chips don't get any topping
items.fix: Spread chips in a single layer on the largest tray you have. Two trays are better than one pile.

items.cause: Grated too coarsely, or pre-packaged anti-caking cheese used
items.fix: Grate fresh cheddar finely. Pre-grated cheese has anti-caking powder that prevents proper melting.

items.cause: Cold toppings added and then left
items.fix: Nachos should go from oven to table in under 2 minutes. Set out all the toppings in bowls before the oven timer goes off, then finish and carry straight to the table.

content.text: The original nacho was created in 1943 by Ignacio Anaya in Piedras Negras, Mexico, from what he had in the kitchen: corn tortilla chips, cheese, and jalapeños. The loaded version expanded into US Tex-Mex restaurant menus during the 1970s and became a stadium food staple. Today the fully loaded nacho, served as a shared plate, is one of the most widely eaten Tex-Mex dishes in Britain.
